data.narrative:
Standard Electron is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Tyler Norwood and Alex Le Roux. The company has raised approximately $3.2M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA), though the peer set includes later-stage players such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method applies meaningfully to this analysis. Using the $3.2M in total capital raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $8M. A peer-median approach was not applicable: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability, falling short of the minimum 3-datapoint threshold required for reliable cross-sectional analysis.

The single applicable method supports a valuation range of $7M to $9M, centered on $8M. This range reflects the moderate step-up assumption embedded in stage-progression analysis; the primary uncertainty stems from the absence of narrow peer validation. Given the sparse same-stage comparability in Climate & Energy at the Seed level and Standard Electron's early-stage capital base, validation of this estimate would benefit materially from additional founder-stage or early-seed transactions in the climate technology subset.
